heroCommands.comment: Install a backend, for example JAX

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Keras 3 is a high-level deep learning framework that runs on top of JAX, TensorFlow or PyTorch (and OpenVINO for inference). You build and train models for vision, language, audio, time series and recommendations with the same simple API, whichever backend you choose.
sixtySeconds.problem: Deep learning code is usually tied to one framework. Keras lets you write models once and run them on the backend that is fastest or best supported for your project, and the README cites speedups of 20% to 350% depending on the backend.
whoFor: PyTorch or JAX users who want a high-level training API
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a friendly, well-documented API that avoids framework lock-in. It's officially supported on Linux and macOS; on Windows the README recommends WSL2.
requirements: One backend: TensorFlow 2.16.1+, JAX 0.4.20+ or PyTorch 2.6.0+

overview: Keras 3 is published on PyPI as keras; Keras 2 remains available as tf-keras. After installing keras you install a backend package and select it with the KERAS_BACKEND environment variable or ~/.keras/keras.json. The backend must be set before importing keras.

It is intended as a drop-in replacement for tf.keras with the TensorFlow backend; models without custom components can run on JAX or PyTorch immediately. Keras models can train on tf.data pipelines or PyTorch DataLoaders, and can be used inside native PyTorch modules or JAX functions.

For GPU support, the repository provides requirements files per backend that install CUDA dependencies through pip, and recommends a clean environment per backend. The OpenVINO backend only supports model.predict().

steps.title: Create a clean environment and install
steps.body: Run inside a clone of the Keras repository. Expects an NVIDIA driver to be installed.
steps.code:
conda create -y -n keras-jax python=3.10
conda activate keras-jax
pip install -r requirements-jax-cuda.txt
python pip_build.py --install
